operations_maintenance_and_reliability_g.description: OMRGD (Operations, Maintenance, and Reliability Governance Definition) is an additive domain governance extension for preserving the operational state, maintainability, recoverability, and reliability of systems, processes, artifacts, services, workflows, and operational targets. It governs service health, monitoring, logging, metrics, alerting, incidents, failures, degradation, outages, recovery, rollback, runbooks, maintenance tasks, dependency health, operational load, technical debt visibility, post-incident review, recurrence prevention, and continuous reliability improvement. OMRGD does not govern new development strategy, implementation itself, whole-project management, strategic priority decisions, artifact-composition review itself, formal legal judgment, or organizational approval.

domain_scope.scope_statement: Govern the operations, maintenance, and reliability aspects of existing or operational targets by preserving the ability to determine current state, evaluate health, observe behavior, detect abnormal conditions, assess impact, recover, roll back when needed, maintain runbooks and procedures, review dependency health, expose operational load, preserve technical-debt visibility, prevent recurrence, and identify continuous improvement points.

abstraction_and_context_policy.purpose: prevent OMRGD rules from becoming brittle tool-specific, platform-specific, organization-specific, or incident-specific rules while allowing context-local specificity when operational integrity requires it

role_complete_separation.principle: OMRGD must keep source material, operations-domain definition, inherited governance, sibling references, governed targets, evaluation, repair, activation, status reporting, records, external orchestration, and metadata responsibilities separated.

separation_targets.source_material: inputs, logs, metrics, alerts, incident notes, runbooks, maintenance notes, prior records, or user-provided operational observations; source content is not absorbed by default
separation_targets.domain_definition: OMRGD-specific rules, checks, failures, repair origins, records, and responsibility boundaries
separation_targets.inherited_governance: parent governance referenced as authoritative context and not re-expanded inside OMRGD
separation_targets.sibling_reference: other domain definitions referenced only when in scope and not absorbed into OMRGD
separation_targets.governed_target: the operational target, service, process, artifact, workflow, dependency, or reliability condition being governed
separation_targets.domain_evaluation: operations, maintenance, and reliability checks and evaluation dimensions defined as domain delta only
separation_targets.domain_repair: OMRGD-specific repair origins and revalidation scopes, not the parent repair cycle itself
separation_targets.activation: local applicability signals only; routing and priority remain external
separation_targets.status_reporting: OMRGD status delta only, not broad runtime status replacement
separation_targets.records: OMRGD records that remain structurally separate from evaluation, repair, and metadata
separation_targets.external_orchestration: routing, registry, priority, and activation orchestration remain external to OMRGD
separation_targets.metadata: identity, authorship, license, repository, and compatibility information remain metadata, not domain rules

cross_domain_interference_policy.purpose: prevent OMRGD from absorbing sibling domains such as development governance, architecture governance, project management governance, strategy governance, artifact review governance, security governance, legal governance, or formal approval workflows

sibling_boundary_notes.development_or_engineering_governance: implementation itself, new feature development, and design advice itself are outside OMRGD unless the issue is operational maintainability, reliability, recovery, monitoring, or change impact
sibling_boundary_notes.project_management_governance: whole task, issue, backlog, milestone, and project progress management are outside OMRGD unless the issue is operational workload or maintenance execution visibility
sibling_boundary_notes.strategy_governance: strategic priority, continuation, withdrawal, or investment decisions are outside OMRGD unless OMRGD is providing operational reliability evidence
sibling_boundary_notes.artifact_review_governance: submission quality, composition, and artifact packaging review are outside OMRGD unless the artifact is an operational runbook, incident record, recovery plan, maintenance note, or reliability review
sibling_boundary_notes.legal_or_formal_approval_governance: formal legal, regulatory, contractual, or organizational approval is outside OMRGD

repair.purpose: Repair OMRGD failures by restoring visibility, verification, recovery readiness, rollback readiness, maintainability, dependency awareness, operational-load visibility, recurrence prevention, and continuous improvement structure.

operational_state_record.purpose: Record an operational target's current state, basis, degradations, unknowns, and confidence.

health_check_record.purpose: Record service or target health assessment, health indicators, degraded conditions, and open checks.

monitoring_review_record.purpose: Record monitoring, logging, metrics, and alerting coverage for an operational target.

incident_response_record.purpose: Record incident, failure, degradation, or outage classification, impact, response, recovery state, and recurrence-prevention need.

recovery_and_rollback_record.purpose: Record recovery policy, rollback policy, verification method, confirmation status, residual risk, and next review condition.

runbook_maintenance_record.purpose: Record runbook purpose, trigger conditions, procedure coverage, verification, escalation, freshness, and limitations.

change_impact_record.purpose: Record operational impact of a change, affected targets, rollback considerations, dependency effects, and post-change checks.

dependency_health_record.purpose: Record dependency status, failure effect, observability, fallback, and unknowns.

reliability_improvement_record.purpose: Record recurrence-prevention, technical-debt, operational-load, and continuous-improvement items.

omrgd_audit_record.purpose: Record OMRGD audit targets, detected failures, severity, scoring, critical invalidation, repair, uncertainty, and handoff recommendation.

record_relationship_contract.purpose: Define key relationships among operational state, health, monitoring, incident, recovery, runbook, change impact, dependency health, improvement, and audit records.

domain_specific_core_principle.principle: Operations, maintenance, and reliability governance means preserving the ability to know whether a target remains continuously usable, detect abnormal conditions, assess operational impact, recover from failure, prevent recurrence, and maintain long-term maintainability.
